subject: problem with discrete / continuous x scale

messages.author: a963405a0585f59a
messages.subject: problem with discrete / continuous x scale
parts:
Hi, I have a plot with three layers, using two data files. One the x
axis I have a discrete variable, "conditon" with three levels.

The geom_bar and geom_errorbar layers are fine.
When I add the geom_point layer from a separate data file (but also
with a discrete variable "condition"), it overlaps with the error bar.
So that they don't overlap I used:

aes(x=as.numeric(condition)-.05, ...)

which nicely moves the data points a little to the left so they don't
overlap the error bars. But this causes a problem later down the track
when I want to change the order that the 3 levels of the condition
variable are displayed in. By default it gives "baseline" on the left,
"opp_dir" in the middle and "same_dir" on the right. But I want to
swap "opp_dir" and "same_dir" around. I do this with:

+ scale_x_discrete(breaks = c
("baseline","same_dir","opp_dir"),limits=c
("baseline","same_dir","opp_dir"),labels = c("no adaptation", "same
direction", "opposite direction"))

which swaps around the labels, bars and error bars appropriately, but
leaves the point data where it was and it is now mislabeled and
doesn't match the bar and error bar data.

If I don't use as.numeric() for the geom_point x scale, the
scale_x_discrete() will move it appropriately. Or, if I leave the
conditions in their default order, everything remains properly matched
and labeled. But I want to be able to BOTH shift the point data and
switch the order of the conditions.

Full code below:

p<-ggplot(data=pses,x=condition,y=pse) + theme_bw()
p<-p +
geom_bar(data=meanPSEsCI,aes(x=condition,y=pse,stat="identity"),color="black",fill=FALSE,position="dodge")
p<-p +
geom_errorbar(data=meanPSEsCI,aes(x=condition,ymin=ci95l,ymax=ci95u),position="dodge",width=0.25)
p<- p+geom_point(data=pses,aes(x=as.numeric(condition)-.
05,y=pse,shape=subject),size=3)+scale_shape(solid=F)
p <- p + scale_x_discrete(breaks = c
("baseline","same_dir","opp_dir"),limits=c
("baseline","same_dir","opp_dir"),labels = c("no adaptation", "same
direction", "opposite direction"))
